question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 22% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is always considered to be 100%.

Selling Price (SP) at 22% profit = 100% + 22% = 122% of CP.

SP = 122% of &rupee;500

SP = 122 × 5 = &rupee;610

**∴ The correct answer is &rupee;610.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = &rupee;500

Profit = 22%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
 CP = &rupee;500
 
 SP = &rupee;610
 

 + 22% Profit
 Profit = &rupee;110
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 500 × (100 + 22) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 500 × 122 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 5 × 122

⇒ SP = &rupee;610

**∴ The correct answer is &rupee;610.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

When an article is sold at a loss, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

If an article goes through multiple transactions with profits P₁% and P₂%, Net Profit% = P₁ + P₂ + (P₁ × P₂) ÷ 100.
